history.period: Unknown (foundation date undocumented in published sources)
history.summary: Important Shakti temple of the Mithila region dedicated to Kankali Mata, a form of Goddess Kali, in the Laxmisagar locality near the historic Rambagh Fort, about 2 km from Darbhanga Junction. Worship was traditionally conducted under the patronage of the Darbhanga royal family and the shrine later opened to the general public; it is noted for tantric forms of worship historically prevalent in Mithila. Detailed foundation records are limited in published sources. Coordinates from the 'Maa Kankali Mandir, Darbhanga Fort' location listing, corroborated by geocoder (Rambagh Fort Gate).

name: Kankali Mata Temple
town_description: Darbhanga is a city in north Bihar and the historic seat of the Darbhanga Raj, regarded as the cultural capital of the Mithila region. It is known for its palaces (now universities), hundreds of ponds, and many temples dedicated to Kali and Durga built by the former kings.

travel.road: Within Darbhanga city; Laxmisagar locality near Rambagh Fort, off Raj Quila Road (Mansaar Colony)

visitor_information.best_time: October-November (Navaratri and Kali Puja draw the biggest crowds)
